desc:
Flutter integrations for payments, analytics and your backend connect your app to the services your business already uses. Ecom Swift LLC sets them up in your own accounts, writes clean code and tests every flow on iOS and Android.

## What are Flutter integrations?

A Flutter integration is the code and configuration that lets your app talk to an outside service. That service might be the App Store and Google Play for purchases, an analytics tool, a push notification provider, an email platform, a crash reporter or your own API.

Most apps need several of these. The app itself shows screens, but the business value often sits in what happens behind them: a payment is recorded, a user is identified, an event is counted, a message arrives on a locked phone.

## Why integrations are easy to get wrong

A demo integration is quick. A reliable one is not. Real users lose signal in a lift, switch apps during a payment, reinstall on a new phone or tap a button twice. Each of those cases needs a decision, and each one is where careless code fails.

Purchases are the clearest example. If a payment succeeds but the app does not enable the feature, you have an unhappy customer and a support ticket. If a subscriber changes phones and cannot restore access, you lose trust. Push notifications, sign-in and analytics each have their own traps, such as missing permissions, wrong keys for one platform or events sent with different names on iOS and Android.

## How well-built integrations affect results

Working integrations turn an app from a screen collection into a business tool. Purchases generate revenue, analytics show which features people use, push messages bring users back, and crash monitoring tells you what broke before reviews do.

The mechanism is trust in the data. When events are named consistently and sent reliably, you can make decisions from them. When purchase state is checked properly, your income matches your records. Tidy integration code also makes the next change cheaper, because each service sits in its own layer rather than being scattered through the screens.

## What a solid integration includes

- Keys and credentials created in your own provider accounts, never in ours.
- Provider code placed in a dedicated layer, so screens do not depend on a specific vendor.
- Platform setup done correctly: entitlements, manifest entries, capabilities and configuration files.
- Error handling for failed calls, timeouts and expired sessions.
- Retry and offline behavior for calls that can wait for a connection.
- Purchase flows that handle pending, cancelled and restored states.
- Analytics events with consistent names and properties on both platforms.
- Push notification registration, permission prompts and token handling.
- Crash and error monitoring that sends useful reports without private data.
- Short setup notes that explain how each service is configured.

## How we connect your services

We begin by listing the services and the user actions they support. We read each provider's current documentation, create or check the accounts and keys with you, and add the packages the provider recommends. When a package does not exist or does not cover your case, we say so and propose a platform-specific bridge.

Then we write the integration code, wire it to the relevant screens and test on real devices, using each provider's sandbox or test mode where it exists. In the Basic package we connect one service. The Standard package covers several services with tested flows and offline handling. The Premium package adds a fuller set, including purchases on both stores, push on both systems and backend sync. You receive working flows and the notes needed to maintain them.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Create the provider accounts in your own name.
- Decide which events you want to measure before we add tracking.
- Test purchases with the sandbox accounts the stores provide.
- Keep a record of which keys belong to testing and which to production.
- Tell us how your backend handles users and errors.

**Avoid:**
- Putting secret keys directly inside the app where users can extract them.
- Sending personal data to analytics without a clear reason.
- Skipping the restore purchases option.
- Treating a working demo as a finished integration.
- Adding services you will not use, since each one adds weight and maintenance.

## Who this service is for

An app owner who has screens but no working payments. A team that needs analytics and crash reporting wired in before a launch. A business with an existing web API that needs its mobile app to read and write the same data.

## What we need from you

The list of services you want connected, access to their dashboards as a team member or developer user, and the app repository as a collaborator. If you have a backend, we need its documentation or an example of its responses. We never ask for passwords. Providers bill you directly, and our price covers the integration work only.
